FIX BUG #378: Two conclude refusals print runs of spaces mid-sentence

You are fixing exactly one bug from the code-health epic (#330) on branch fix-378-conclude-text, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text is below and is the whole framing: its "Fix" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Where the issue says the operator rules between options, implement the option the issue recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say in your result notes which option you took so the pull request can ask for the ruling.

RULES
- Scope: fix this bug and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites.
- Tests: add or extend the suite that proves the fix. Assert exact values and exact error variants or text, never is_err() alone. Show every new test binds: make a compiling mutation that removes the fix, run the test and see it fail, restore the fix, and record the failing test name in your notes.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new line and branch reachable by a test. If a branch cannot be reached deterministically, restructure rather than leave it uncovered.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Gates before you report complete, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test for every crate you touched (crate-scoped: cargo test -p <crate>); git diff --check.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#378)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.

THE ISSUE (#378), verbatim:

Found by the code-health sweep (epic #330). Verified on `main` at `ba52724e` (2026-09-25).

## What happens

Two operator-facing refusal messages in `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs` contain long runs of spaces mid-sentence. The `\` line continuations were lost when the lines were folded:

- `engine.rs:3379`: `"conclude: run '{run_id}' refused the stop ({refusal}); the                  journal moved beneath the conclusion, so something may still                  be driving this run — …"` (18-space runs)
- `engine.rs:3448`: `"conclude: the journal moved beneath the conclusion of run '{run_id}',              so something may still be driving it — …"` (14-space runs)

The tests (`conclude_tests.rs`) assert only `.contains(...)`, so they pass anyway.

## Why it matters

This is the text an operator reads when a conclude is refused, which is exactly when something may still be driving the run.

## Fix

Restore the `\` continuations, and add one exact-text assertion (or a no-double-space assertion) for each message.

## Acceptance

- Both messages render on single-spaced lines, and a test pins the exact text.
